title: When the Autopsy Sings
premise: When the coffin of Hollow Creek's beloved founder, Augustus Wren, is found empty during a routine exhumation, night-shift taxi dispatcher Emrys Dravenmoor realizes the dispatch logs she's kept for years contain coded entries pointing to a decades-old cover-up. As she decodes the ledger hidden in the town's own street addresses and fare records, Emrys uncovers that Wren faked his death to escape blackmail by the founding families—and that her missing mother was the last person to drive him. At the anniversary dinner where the town plans to honor Wren's memory, Emrys must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the makeshift family of drivers who took her in; she chooses truth, but negotiates a confession that spares the innocent, finally stepping out of the shadows she built around herself.
about_author: E. M. Underhill spent six years answering phones for a small-town cab company before turning those graveyard shifts into fiction. They write mysteries about people the world overlooks, from a drafty apartment above a laundromat.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Called in on her night off to log an official run, Emrys witnesses the exhumation of founder Augustus Wren—and the coffin comes up empty. The crowd murmurs; the mayor goes pale. Emrys, invisible as always behind her clipboard, notices one detail no one else does: the grave dirt has been disturbed recently, from below. Beat: cold fascination masking old grief.

chapters.title: Fare Records and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Back at the dispatch office, Emrys compulsively rereads her archived logs and finds an anomaly: three fares to Wren's mausoleum road the week he 'died'—logged under a driver ID belonging to her mother, who vanished twenty-five years ago. Her hands shake. Beat: the past knocking on a door she sealed shut.

chapters.title: The Drivers' Table
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Sunday dinner at the home of veteran driver Marisol Vega, where the misfit cab company gathers like family. Emrys almost tells them about the ledger clue but swallows it, protecting them out of habit. Marisol senses something wrong and presses gently; Emrys deflects. Beat: warmth that hurts because she can't let herself need it.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Researching at the library, Emrys finds the official history of Wren's death doesn't match weather records, road closures, or her own dispatch tapes. The librarian, Mr. Okafor, quietly slips her a box of unindexed town archives—the first person to offer help unprompted. Beat: cautious hope; allies might exist.

chapters.title: Code in the Grid
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Late-night breakthrough: the founding families named the streets after themselves, and the fare ledger's odd entries map onto those names—a cipher. Decoded fragments reference 'the debt,' 'the girl,' and 'the anniversary.' Someone has been maintaining this code for decades, and recent entries exist. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Smile
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Summoned to city hall to 'verify dispatch records' for the anniversary ceremony, Emrys meets Mayor Corliss Hale, who is charming, watchful, and asks one question too many about her mother. Emrys lies smoothly and hates how good she's gotten at it. Beat: the hunter realizing she's also being hunted.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol remembers the night Emrys's mother disappeared—a fare she refused to take, a warning she didn't pass on. Guilt has ridden shotgun for twenty-five years. She decides to tell Emrys everything, then loses her nerve when Emrys arrives looking so much like her mother. Beat: love tangled in cowardice.

chapters.title: Grave Shift
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys breaks into the mausoleum and finds Wren's crypt hollowed out long ago, with fresh tire tracks and a modern padlock. Inside: a second ledger page confirming Wren is alive—or was until very recently. Footsteps force her to hide; she escapes through a maintenance tunnel. Beat: terror transmuted into certainty.

chapters.title: The Debt
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Decoded fully, the ledger reveals the founding families covered up a fatal fire at the Wren mill in 1962, blaming a dead worker. Wren's 'death' was his escape from their blackmail—but he kept paying, and someone kept collecting. The final entry names a drop point: the anniversary dinner itself. Beat: the scale of the lie revealed.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Cab
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A black sedan tails Emrys between runs. She uses her knowledge of the grid to lose it, then finds a note on her windshield: 'STOP DIGGING. YOUR MOTHER DIDN'T.' Shaken, she nearly burns the ledger—then realizes the threat confirms her mother is alive too. Beat: fear weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Confessions Over Coffee
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finally tells Emrys about the refused fare and the warning note her mother left behind—which Marisol kept all these years. Emrys reads her mother's handwriting for the first time since childhood and weeps without sound. Beat: the found family deepens; guilt met with forgiveness neither expected.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Cross-referencing dates, Emrys discovers 'the girl' in the code was her mother—not a witness to the fire, but the mill owner's daughter who survived it. Her mother wasn't hiding from the families; she was hiding Wren himself. Emrys's whole childhood of abandonment reframes as protection. Beat: fury and relief colliding.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The town gears up for Wren's centennial dinner; the cab company gets the contract for every dignitary run. Emrys maneuvers herself into dispatching the head table's cars, giving her eyes on every founding-family member. Corliss Hale watches her a beat too long. Beat: the trap being set, by both sides.

chapters.title: Okafor's Warning
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor's POV. The librarian admits he's been tracking the archive thefts for years—pages removed, microfilm 'lost'—all pointing to the Hale family. He gives Emrys the last intact record and begs her to go to the state police instead of the dinner. She refuses; the drop happens tomorrow night. Beat: mentor's fear versus protégé's momentum.

chapters.title: Roadblock
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hours before the dinner, Emrys is suspended from dispatch on fabricated grounds—someone inside the company talked. She suspects sweet, indebted dispatcher Theo, whose brother works for the Hales. Confronting him, she finds him terrified, not treacherous. Beat: betrayal suspected, loyalty complicated, time bleeding away.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol and the drivers, refusing to let Emrys face this alone, reassign routes to smuggle her into the country club kitchen as a 'caterer's ride-along.' Small acts of quiet rebellion across the dispatch board. Beat: the found family choosing her back, no questions asked.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Amid toasts to a dead man, Emrys watches the drop: Corliss Hale passes an envelope to a bent, familiar figure slipping in through the service door—Augustus Wren, alive, ancient, and done running. Emrys photographs everything, then steps into the light, ending her own invisibility. Beat: the moment of no return.

chapters.title: Glasses Raised, Masks Off
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Confronted before the assembled founders, Emrys plays the ledger aloud—names, dates, the fire, the dead worker's name. Panic fractures the room; Corliss orders her seized, but the drivers arrive en masse, standing shoulder to shoulder. Wren raises his glass and confesses. Beat: chaos, courage, the truth spoken in public.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (interlude). In a police interview room, Wren explains: surviving meant letting everyone believe he was dead, including the girl who saved him—Emrys's mother, who drove him out the night of the staged death and never came home. He shows Emrys the letters her mother sent him for years. Beat: the price of survival made human.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following the letters' postmarks, Emrys traces her mother to a coastal town two states away—alive, retired, terrified. Their reunion is awkward, angry, unfinished: twenty-five years can't be decoded in an afternoon. But her mother gives her the original cipher key and says, 'You were never supposed to be alone.' Beat: love against duty, unresolved but begun.

chapters.title: Sentences and Settlements
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weeks later: the Hales fall, Wren accepts a reduced sentence for obstruction, the mill fire victims' families receive restitution and their true story. Emrys declines a hero's platform, returning to dispatch—but now the drivers save her a seat at the table without asking. Beat: justice imperfect, belonging chosen.

chapters.title: Night Shift, First Light
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On a quiet dawn shift, Emrys logs one last entry in the old cipher—her mother's address, marked 'delivered'—and closes the ledger for good. Sunrise hits the dispatch window as the morning drivers clock in, calling her name like it belongs to them. Beat: the invisible woman, seen at last; the case closed, the life opened.
